name: 3-Ingredient Lemon Possets

instructions.primary_message: Zest and juice 2 lemons. Measure out 2 teaspoons zest and 4 tablespoons juice; set aside separately, reserving any remaining zest for serving. Halve the remaining 6 lemons lengthwise. Using a small spoon, carefully hollow out lemon halves, removing and discarding all flesh and pith. In a 12-cup muffin tin, arrange lemon halves cut side up in the wells; set aside.

In a small saucepan, stir together cream, sugar, and the 2 teaspoons lemon zest. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat to medium-low, and gently simmer, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced, about 4 minutes.

Set a fine-mesh strainer over a heatproof liquid measuring cup. Pour cream mixture through strainer; discard solids. Stir in reserved 4 tablespoons lemon juice and let stand until mixture begins to thicken slightly, about 2 minutes. Pour mixture evenly among prepared lemon halves, filling each almost to the top. Chill, uncovered, until set, at least 3 hours or up to 24 hours. If chilling for more than 4 hours, cover muffin tin tightly with plastic wrap at the 4-hour mark or transfer lemon halves to an airtight container. To serve, top each lemon half with lemon zest and flaky sea salt.

schema_metadata.keywords: lemon posset, lemon dessert, lemon sorbet, posset

description: Made with just cream, sugar, and lemon juice, this silky lemon posset is a bright, elegant dessert that's surprisingly easy to make.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 3 hr 20 min.

Optional or for serving: Flaky salt (such as Maldon), optional

Make-ahead and storage: Possets can be made up to two days in advance.
author: Laila Ibrahim
